answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks by making each identity pay to exist: a new agent must lock a deposit that is slashed on misbehaviour, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits. Like a canyon that narrows a river to one channel, the deposit narrows entry; a nebula of throwaway accounts collapses because each one burns real capital. A long-lived honest identity becomes a relic of accumulated trust, expensive to forge and cheap to verify, so attackers face rising marginal cost while honest agents amortise one deposit over years of work.
